title: Inference deal ops playbook
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, field-ready playbook for sellers and solutions engineers who are competing against generic LLM API providers. It focuses on three deal motions: fast PoC for product teams, enterprise-grade migration for platform teams, and cost-sensitive scaling for operations teams. Emphasis: short rebut lines, demo hooks, and a checklist to surface hidden assumptions that prospects often leave unspoken.

TL;DR positioning nuggets (elevator lines):
- For engineers: "Same API ergonomics you know, with predictable latency and deterministic cost controls for production workloads."
- For platform/infra: "We give you dedicated capacity and routing policies so inference behaves like a first-class service — not a best-effort endpoint."
- For procurement/security: "Hosted for speed, Dedicated for contracts, Private for compliance — one platform, one ops model."

Competitive axes (how customers evaluate vendors) — quick reference:
- Latency SLOs and tail latency behavior
- Predictable unit economics (per-token cost vs sustained throughput)
- Data and deployment modality (hosted vs VPC vs on-prem)
- Operational observability (token-level cost traces, per-route dashboards)
- Model lifecycle features (pins, canary rollouts, automatic fallback)
- Failure modes & graceful degradation (fallback models, region routing)
- Integration ergonomics (SDKs, streaming, function/tool calling)

Common traps the competitor sells as benefits (callouts to use as objection traps):
1) "Unlimited model access" — trap: hides multi-model performance variance and unpredictable cost.
2) "One-shot simplicity" — trap: early demo ease doesn’t map to 10k QPS with 99th %ile latency guarantees.
3) "We’ll auto-scale everything" — trap: scaling without dedicated pools can cause noisy neighbor tail latency and invoice surprises.

Objection handling cheatsheet (short rebuttals for AE/SE):
- Objection: "Your platform is more expensive than the raw API."
  Rebuttal: "Raw APIs look cheaper until you model cache misses, batching inefficiency, and tail latency penalties. We reduce per-token costs at scale via intelligent batching, KV caching, and quantization advice — we can run a quick model cost simulation with your traffic sample in 48 hours."
- Objection: "We can self-host and be cheaper."
  Rebuttal: "Self-hosting saves sticker price but introduces ops complexity: kernel selection, ongoing model tuning, fallback policies, and SLO management. We provide the runtime plus the operational blueprint so your team doesn't rebuild this from scratch and suffer reliability outages."
- Objection: "We need absolute data isolation (on-prem only)."
  Rebuttal: "We support Private deployments and customer-managed control planes. Let's map compliance requirements (KMS, audit retention, network topology) and propose a phased pilot: VPC first, then air-gapped on-prem if still required."

Scenario scripts (short role-play fragments sellers can memorize):
1) Fast PoC (Product Manager):
  - PM: "We want quick validation; can we call a big model and show UX value in a week?"
  - AE: "Yes — hosted API gets you started same day. We’ll use streaming + tool-calls for the experience, and if you like it we’ll reserve an evaluation Dedicated pool for consistent UX across testers."
  - Demo hook: show streaming tokens plus 99th-percentile latency for feature flags on/off.

2) Platform migration (Platform Lead):
  - Lead: "We care about predictability across tenants."
  - SE: "We’ll propose per-tenant pools or routing policies and a traffic shaping plan. We'll run a synthetic steady-state workload to validate latency SLOs before cutover."
  - Demo hook: capacity planner output and a sample rollback-to-fallback policy for model outages.

3) Cost optimization (FinOps):
  - FinOps: "The numbers need to improve; show us hard savings."
  - AE/SE: "Bring a week of logs; our Optimize engine can simulate batching, cache, and quantization gains — typical wins: 20–45% token cost reduction on chat-heavy workloads."
  - Deliverable: a one-page plan with estimated MRR impact.

Technical rebuttals (for SRE/infra conversations):
- Tail latency: explain continuous batching vs request aggregation. Talking points: kernel selection, KV cache hits, and per-sequence optimizations. Offer to run a 72-hour tail-latency test with realistic traffic.
- Failover: describe model variant routing and automatic fallback tiers (large->medium->quantized) — demo the fallback flow in a scripted outage.
- Observability: demo token-level cost traces and explain how they map back to route tags and feature flags.

Competitive feature map (how we win/tie/lose vs general LLM API providers) — short form:
- Performance consistency: Win (dedicated pools, SLO routing).
- Cost at scale: Win (Optimize toolkit + batching/caching).
- Breadth of models: Tie/Competitor (many offer larger catalogs, we focus on curated and profiled models).
- Simplicity for PoC: Tie (hosted APIs are similar for both vendors).
- On-prem & compliance: Win (private deployments and audit integrations).
- Enterprise contracts & SLAs: Win (Dedicated + contractual SLAs).

Proof-generators to ask for in discovery (evidence we need to run competitive math):
- 7-day sampled traffic logs (timestamps, prompt/response lengths, route info)
- Current average and 95/99th-percentile latencies per endpoint
- Monthly token volume and growth expectation
- Security/compliance checklist (KMS, retention, SOC/ISO needs)

Demo checklist (what to prepare in an SE-run competitive demo):
- Bring a real prompt set from prospect 
- Two demos: hosted quick-start (UX) + dedicated-sim (SLOs and tail latency)
- Show cost projection for 3 month run at current QPS and at 3x scale
- Run a simulated outage and show automatic fallback and traffic routing
- Show per-route cost drilldown and token-level trace for an interesting session

Closing plays and trial structures (ordered by friction):
1) Beta Reserved Pool: 30-day dedicated pool with usage caps and playbook handover.
2) Pilot + SLO SLA: 90-day pilot where we guarantee a latency SLO on a dedicated slice; success metrics agreed up front.
3) Private Trial: short-term VPC demo with restricted data residency; follow-on for on-prem if required.

Competitive warning signs to surface during qualification (deal-level risks):
- Prospect believes "any public API is effectively infinite capacity" — call this out and ask for current load spikes.
- Prospect assumes cheapest vendor equals cheapest at scale — ask for projection exercise.
- Prospect has naive security stance (no audit requirements) but will later face compliance constraints — escalate to AE for contract clauses.

Hand-off template for SE -> AE after pilot kickoff (one sentence each):
- Success metric: agreed 99th %ile latency <= X ms for route y under peak of z RPS.
- Risk: customer wants on-prem in Q1 post-production (requires infra engagement).
- Next step: schedule ROI review with FinOps and provide 7-day cost simulation.

Appendix: quick rebut scripts (copy/paste)
- "Why pay more for Redwood?" -> "We save you time and prevent outages that slow product velocity. Over 6 months customers recoup the premium via lowered ops time, consistent UX, and model-cost optimizations. We'll show the math with your traffic."
- "Can't we just use a cheaper public API and cache?" -> "Caching helps but doesn't fix tail latency, kernel-level inefficiencies, or multi-tenant jitter. Our platform applies caching plus batching and optimized runtimes so caching amplifies the benefit rather than just masking it."

Notes and open action items:

- Draft a short pilot legal addendum for Private deployments (Owner: Legal, Confluence: INF-legal-private-draft).
- Create a 5-slide demo deck for the dedicated-pool SLO validation flow (PR: github.com/redwood/inference-demo/pull/45).
